Change c0508. Location: 1818 Vol. III, Ch. VII; 1831 Ch. XXIV.

Context before (unchanged): He seems to feel his own worth, and the greatness of his fall.

1818 text: "When younger," said he, "I felt as if I were destined for some great enterprise.

1831 text: "When younger," said he, "I believed myself destined for some great enterprise.

Diff: " When younger, " said he, " I [-felt as if I were-] {+believed myself+} destined for some great enterprise.

Context after (unchanged): My feelings are profound; but I possessed a coolness of judgment that fitted me for illustrious achievements.

result.rationale: "I felt as if I were destined" becomes "I believed myself destined": the sense of destiny is shifted from a vague feeling to a conviction held by Victor, and the phrasing reads as more self-deceived. The destined-ness remains, but its epistemic status changes.
